name: Scientific pressing / Soviet school
scopeNote: Soviet school: systematic pressing, conditioning, zonal collective play and data-driven preparation. Origin: Viktor Maslov at Dynamo Kyiv (1964-70; 4-4-2 without wingers, zones instead of man-marking, pressing, nutrition/recovery) - Maslov is not a catalog id, recorded here only. Development: Valeriy Lobanovskyi with Anatoliy Zelentsov (Dynamo from 1973, second spell 1984-90, USSR 1982-88). profilePeriod start 1964 and end 1990 are partial years because the exact days were not found; period uses partial dates (Maslov appointment 1964 and Lobanovskyi's 1990 departure not pinned to the day in pages read). Terms used by sources: 'pressing', 'zonal marking', 'universality'/interchangeability, 'system football', 'coalition actions', 'scientific'. 'Total football' is a popular label for Lobanovskyi (Hard Tackle) but Spielverlagerung/TFT frame it as a parallel, systematic and data-driven school, so the evidence supports 'scientific/systematic pressing' rather than 'Soviet Total Football'. Exemplars: valeriy-lobanovskyi, dynamo-kyiv-1974-75, dynamo-kyiv-1985-86.

exemplars.reason: Made science, statistics and data central; Dynamo 1973-90, USSR 1988 Euro finalists.
Cup Winners' Cup and Super Cup 1975; pressed from the off but sat deep vs Bayern.
Cup Winners' Cup 1986, 3-0 v Atletico; rough 4-3-1-2 with sweeper Baltacha.

openQuestions: Exemplars differ: 1975 Dynamo is described as 'a rough' interchangeable system with Blokhin and Onyshchenko up front (TFT) or 4-1-3-2 (Hard Tackle), 1986 Dynamo as a rough 4-3-1-2 with a sweeper (Baltacha), USSR 1986-88 as two lines of four in 4-4-2 (Spielverlagerung). Maslov's original is a 4-4-2 with a holder and a playmaker. Shape is therefore not constant across the idea.

Marking: Maslov 'abolished man-marking in favour of zones' (TFT, retrospective) but Lobanovskyi used man-coverage on Gullit at Euro 1988 (Spielverlagerung). Zonal is the default of the school, with opponent-specific exceptions.

Pressing intensity differed by match: pressed from the off in 1975 final, sat deep and countered vs Bayern (Super Cup 1975) and used a low block vs Ireland 1988. Pressing is the base but not unconditional.

Label: Hard Tackle calls Lobanovskyi's flexibility 'Total Football'; TFT says Maslov's interchangeable side was the groundwork for Totaalvoetbal. Treat 'total football' as a loose comparison; Engelsberg and Spielverlagerung stress system, dialectic and statistics. Credit for inventing pressing is contested (TFT: some credit Michels or Happel's Feyenoord 1970; sport-express and ESPN credit Maslov); the sources are popular-history retrospectives, not 1960s documents.

Maslov vs Lobanovskyi on science: Maslov already stressed fitness, nutrition and recovery; Engelsberg says Lobanovskyi was the first to make science, statistics and data analysis central. Credit for 'scientific' is Lobanovskyi/Zelentsov's, for 'pressing and 4-4-2' Maslov's.
Origin of the Maslov-Lobanovskyi falling-out is unclear (tactical disagreement, personal, or apocryphal vodka story); not essential to the idea.

Spell dates not pinned: Lobanovskyi appointed Dynamo 1973 (Oct 1973 per a search summary only), left 1990; Maslov at Dynamo 1964-70 (sacked 1970, TFT). Statistical evidence is retrospective; no 1970s match data (Opta-type) read.

Stated view dates are approximate periods (original dates not found); mostly attributed via Engelsberg; primary text of Endless Match and the Lobanovskyi-Zelentsov book not read. Russian/Ukrainian searches gave only summaries (sports.ru, 403).

sources.evidence: he built a 4-4-2, outnumbering the two-man midfield across the world, but not hindering his side's creativity at the same time.

sources.title: Viktor Maslov: the pioneer of the 4-4-2 who took pressing to a new level (These Football Times)

sources.title: Team Analysis: Valeriy Lobanovskyi's USSR (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: they were essentially a team built around two lines of four. Working in a 4-4-2 shape, they were usually concerned about the space they had to cover.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Valeriy Lobanovskyi's USSR (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Lobanovskyi was a strong believer of the idea that the best way to overcome rivals is to manipulate the size of the playing area, making the field larger when in possession and smaller when defending. In order to do that, full-backs and wingers usually provided width by moving upfield.

statedView.quote: It is impossible to rely on luck […] in modern football. It is necessary to create an ensemble, a collective of believers who subordinate themselves to the common playing idea.
If an opponent has adjusted himself to our style of play […] then we need to find a new strategy. That is the dialectic of the game.
Games fade from the memory, but results stay.
Football is like an aeroplane. As velocities increase, so does air resistance, so you have to make the head more streamlined. (Maslov, via Wilson, Inverting the Pyramid)

influences.note: Parallel and compared school; Maslov's interchangeable side is called groundwork for Totaalvoetbal (TFT). Pressing and zones also feed later gegenpressing.
